                    ### Question
                    An 11-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents because of a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, followed by a facial rash 4 days later. The facial rash did not involve the perioral skin. Her temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F). A photograph of the rash on her lower arms is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Rubella
opb. Erythema infectiosum
opc. Hand, foot, and mouth disease
opd. Exanthem subitum
ope. Scarlet fever

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely diagnosis for the 11-year-old girl with a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities, along with a recent history of fever and rash, is Rubella. The presentation of a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, headache, followed by a facial rash without perioral involvement fits the classic description of Rubella. The absence of perioral involvement helps differentiate it from other viral exanthems like Erythema infectiosum and Exanthem subitum.
